answer: An agent economy can price identity creation with a refundable hardware-backed deposit: each agent locks a stake issued by a trusted enclave that holds only one identity per device cluster. Like saffron graded by color intensity, the deposit's risk weight rises when peers detect behavioral anomalies. A quill signature binds every action to that deposit, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents build a reef of mutual endorsements that release deposits over time, while detected sockpuppets forfeit theirs - the attacker pays linearly per fake identity.
